title: Compliance
summary: Compliance ensures adherence to applicable regulations and internal policies through continuous Monitoring & Assurance (including mystery shopping) and a calendar-driven compliance program yielding timely, auditable disclosures. It enforces consumer protection, data privacy, and robust data governance with mandatory privacy training, plus a fully automated KYC/AML onboarding framework with real-time identity verification and ongoing due diligence, all while aligning with multi-layer regulatory oversight, internal solvency/capital models, and periodic regulator reporting to demonstrate financial resilience and ongoing compliance.

guidance_context.topic_description: Compliance encompasses key regulatory and governance processes within insurance operations.

nodes.title: Customer Onboarding
nodes.summary: Implementing a Know Your Customer framework for insurance onboarding harmonizes regulatory requirements with robust identity verification and KYC controls to establish verifiable customer profiles from day one. It enables digital onboarding with streamlined verification, enhanced data quality, and ongoing due diligence, while upholding privacy protections and AML/CFT compliance.

guidance_context.parent_topic_description: Customer Management handles onboarding, KYC, and customer data processes.

nodes.title: Regulatory Framework
nodes.summary: The section outlines the regulatory frameworks governing the insurance industry and the company’s internal compliance program to ensure ongoing adherence. Oversight is multi-layered—state, federal, and international regulators—with jurisdiction-specific requirements for solvency, capital, governance, and market conduct; the company uses internal models to monitor solvency and capital adequacy and conducts periodic reporting to regulators and stakeholders to demonstrate financial resilience and regulatory compliance.

guidance_context.parent_topic_description: Compliance encompasses key regulatory and governance processes within insurance operations.

title: Operations
summary: Claims management delivers end-to-end processing from FNOL through coverage verification, triage and adjuster assignment, analytics-driven SIU investigations, a defined settlement workflow with supervisory approvals and compliant payments, and post-settlement subrogation and closure with ongoing reserve monitoring. Onboarding centers on a centralized CRM with secure API-sharing to policy and claims platforms, enforceable data governance, ongoing quality checks, and a five-step digital onboarding flow to optimize the first-year experience. Analytics provides fraud oversight via real-time dashboards and monthly loss/recovery reporting, while policy lifecycle management optimizes applications, renewals, and terminations with governance, automation, refunds rules, lienholder notifications, and regulatory archival.

guidance_context.parent_topic_description: Operations manages claims processing, settlement, fraud detection, and recovery activities.

nodes.title: Claims Management
nodes.summary: Claims Management starts with FNOL, capturing incident and policy data, verifying coverage, and triaging by severity, type, and complexity to assign to the appropriate adjuster with authority and reserves; SIUs conduct fraud investigations using analytics, surveillance, interviews, and digital forensics, coordinating with law enforcement as needed. The settlement workflow prescribes defined steps, required documentation, and supervisory approval for offers above thresholds, with payments issued via approved methods (EFT/ACH or checks) in compliance with state timelines. Subrogation seeks recovery from responsible third parties post-settlement, with legal counsel and recovery tracking, and closure finalizes the claim after all payments are made, while ongoing monitoring for audits, reserve adequacy, and management review of reopened claims occurs.

guidance_context.parent_topic_description: Operations manages claims processing, settlement, fraud detection, and recovery activities.

nodes.title: Subrogation
nodes.summary: The subrogation process involves the insurer seeking reimbursement from third parties responsible for a loss after settling a claim, using legal counsel and tracking recovery against the claim payment.

guidance_context.sub_topic_description: Supports recovery from liable third parties after claim settlement.
guidance_context.parent_topic_description: Operations manages claims processing, settlement, fraud detection, and recovery activities.

nodes.title: Customer Data Management
nodes.summary: On onboarding, customer data is captured and stored in a centralized CRM. It is securely shared with policy and claims platforms through APIs to support underwriting, policy administration, and claims processing, while enforcing data governance. Ongoing data quality checks ensure accuracy, completeness, and integrity across the CRM and downstream systems.

guidance_context.sub_topic_description: Manages storage and protection of customer data.
guidance_context.parent_topic_description: Customer Management handles onboarding, KYC, and customer data processes.

nodes.title: Customer Onboarding
nodes.summary: Insurance digital onboarding follows a five-step flow, with the average completion time used to monitor and improve efficiency. To boost the first-year experience, the framework recommends proactive engagement and welcome communication packs to ensure timely activation and ongoing customer touchpoints.

guidance_context.parent_topic_description: Customer Management handles onboarding, KYC, and customer data processes.

nodes.title: Policy Lifecycle
nodes.summary: Policy lifecycle management centers on efficiently handling application, renewal, and termination processes across all lines, ensuring accurate data, timely underwriting, and compliant administration. By optimizing renewals and terminations, insurers improve profitability through better retention, pricing integrity, and lapse control while maintaining high customer satisfaction with seamless experiences. Robust governance, automation, and cross-functional controls throughout the lifecycle ensure regulatory compliance and audit readiness.

guidance_context.sub_topic_description: Covers onboarding journey and underwriting fraud prevention.
guidance_context.parent_topic_description: Policy Lifecycle covers underwriting, issuance, amendments, and termination processes.

nodes.title: Policy Termination
nodes.summary: POLICY TERMINATION specifies the triggers and steps to terminate an insurance policy, including the rules for refund calculation (e.g., short-rate versus pro-rata) and the cancellation workflow. It also requires timely notification of lienholders, updating core systems to reflect termination, and compliant archival/retention of records per regulatory requirements.

guidance_context.sub_topic_description: Handles policy termination and lifecycle completion.
guidance_context.parent_topic_description: Policy Lifecycle covers underwriting, issuance, amendments, and termination processes.

title: Policy Lifecycle
summary: Policy origination spans the creation of new policies from application through underwriting evaluation to issuance, with automated and manual steps allocated by risk factors and complexity. Policy administration handles mid-term amendments that modify coverage or payment methods, triggering re-rating and a revised premium statement with endorsements documented as addenda; the renewal process re-evaluates risk at expiration using updated exposure, claims history, and external factors to determine premium adjustments and renewal offers or non-renewals, supported by retention strategies such as loyalty discounts, streamlined renewals, and predictive analytics-driven proactive outreach.

guidance_context.sub_topic_description: Covers onboarding journey and underwriting fraud prevention.
guidance_context.parent_topic_description: Policy Lifecycle covers underwriting, issuance, amendments, and termination processes.

title: Product Management
summary: Product management for commercial property insurance defines the coverage types and endorsements and enforces a formal development/modification lifecycle that requires cross-functional approvals from underwriting, actuarial, legal/compliance, product management, and distribution to ensure regulatory compliance, sound pricing, and market suitability. The Insurance Product Catalog serves as the reference for all offerings, detailing coverage frameworks, terms and exclusions, and mapping products to target market segments, underwriting criteria, and distribution channels to guide pricing, risk assessment, regulatory alignment, line management, and sales enablement.
